verdict.rationale: The evidence documents one first-party rule-to-action mechanism. AWS Budgets lets you set cost thresholds (actual or forecasted) and take automatic action when they are crossed, such as applying an IAM policy that blocks new provisioning. That trigger is limited to cost and usage events, and nothing in the pack shows a general event-rule engine. CLI scripting and Lambda's serverless description are building blocks, not rule-triggered automation, so they earn no credit. Missing for 10: a general-purpose event rules/routing service (e.g. arbitrary service events triggering targets), documented event sources beyond budgets, AI-native or agent-driven rule definition, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
